Bootstrap-Based Stability Estimation for Label Propagation

Source: R/label_propagation.R
label_spreading_bootstrap.Rd

Memory-conscious bootstrap stability estimation for label spreading

Usage

label_spreading_bootstrap(
  adj,
  labels,
  refer = NULL,
  alpha = 0.8,
  sample_rate = 0.8,
  sample_n = 50,
  backend = c("blocked", "dense"),
  block_size = 128,
  tol = 0.001,
  max_iter = 100,
  epsilon = 0,
  refer_h5 = NULL,
  tmpdir = tempdir(),
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

adj

A square adjacency matrix (preferably sparse) representing the graph.

labels

An integer vector of length equal to the number of nodes. Use `NA` for unlabeled entries.

refer

Optional dense reference soft-label matrix (N x C). This legacy argument is supported only by backend = "dense". If supplied while backend is omitted, the function selects the dense backend with a warning.

alpha

Float in (0, 1). The propagation coefficient controlling the balance between prior and propagated labels (default: 0.9).

sample_rate

Fraction of labeled nodes used in each bootstrap sample (default: 0.8).

sample_n

Number of bootstrap replicates (default: 50).

backend

Bootstrap implementation. The default is "blocked"; use "dense" only for small inputs or legacy reproduction.

block_size

Number of label classes processed in one HDF5-backed block.

tol

Convergence threshold (default: 1e-3).

max_iter

Maximum number of iterations for propagation (default: 100).

epsilon

Small prior assigned to unlabeled entries (default: 0).

refer_h5

Optional reusable HDF5 reference for the blocked backend. A caller-supplied file is never deleted by this function.

tmpdir

Directory for temporary HDF5 files used by the blocked backend.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print progress and convergence status (default: TRUE).

...

Additional arguments passed to label_spreading() when backend = "dense".

Value

A list with prob, the full-reference probability matrix, and deviance, the per-cell mean L1 bootstrap deviation.

Details

Repeatedly applies label spreading to subsampled label sets and returns the full-label probability estimate together with a node-level bootstrap deviance. The default backend = "blocked" processes label classes in bounded blocks and streams intermediate matrices through HDF5. This avoids retaining a full cells-by-label matrix for every concurrent bootstrap.

The blocked backend still returns one dense cells-by-label probability matrix for compatibility. Its peak memory therefore includes that final matrix, the sparse graph, and one class block per concurrent worker. Reduce the number of future workers when either the cell count or clone count is large. The former dense implementation remains available with backend = "dense" for small inputs and reproducibility checks.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
adj <- Matrix::rsparsematrix(100, 100, density = 0.05)
labels <- rep(NA, 100)
labels[1:10] <- sample(1:3, 10, replace = TRUE)
result <- label_spreading_bootstrap(adj, labels, block_size = 32)
str(result)
} # }
